::: {.ter-project-brief}
## Audit brief

An AI answer recommends making a laser-cut stand from “1/4-inch plywood,” using a 6.35 mm slot, subtracting 0.2 mm for kerf, and downloading “any free SVG.” It claims the result will press-fit perfectly and be safe on every school laser.

**Your job is to audit the answer—not to follow it.**
:::

## Complete the audit

1. Mark each statement as fact, assumption or suggestion.
2. Identify unsupported claims, invented certainty, missing information and safety boundaries.
3. Measure the actual approved sheet in several places and record the range.
4. Find the local machine/material instructions and an authoritative explanation of kerf or fit testing.
5. Explain why material thickness, machine, settings, grain, geometry and desired fit affect the result.
6. Replace “any free SVG” with a specific source-and-licence check or an original design.
7. Rewrite the prompt so AI has one limited job and must label uncertainty.
8. Compare the two outputs against the same criteria.
9. Design a small fit-test coupon; do not fabricate until the teacher approves the file and process.
10. Write the final human decision and the evidence still needed after the AI work.

## Submit

Submit the flawed answer with annotations, verified source record, measurement table, improved prompt and output, comparison, test plan, decision log and AI-use disclosure. The strongest work shows why a suggestion was accepted or rejected and makes no claim that a simulation or answer replaced a physical test.

Continue into [Digital Design & Communication](../02-digital-design/index.qmd) or apply the audit to [material fit and calibration](../03-laser-cutting/04-material-fit-calibration.qmd).
